<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
Assume the hypotheses $\mathrm{(Tam)}$, $\mathrm{(H^0)}$  with the discriminant $-D_K<-3$ such that $(D_K,pN)=1$.
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item If $E/\mathbb{Q}$ has good ordinary reduction at $p$, assume the hypotheses (1) - (5) in \S \ref{sec:ord}.
        \item  If $E/\mathbb{Q}$ has supersingular reduction at $p$, assume the hypotheses (1) - (6) in \S \ref{sec:supersingular}.
    \end{enumerate}
Then
$\mathrm{Fitt}_{\Lambda_n}\left(\operatorname{Sel}^{\emptyset, 0}\big(K_n, E[p^\infty])\big)^\vee\right)$  is the principal ideal generated by the square of a BDP analogue of theta element $\theta_{n}(f)$ which is explicitly  defined as a collection of the values of the corresponding $p$-adic modular forms at CM points in \S \ref{def_theta} in $\Lambda_n$.
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
Let  $B$ be a $\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}$-algebra, $k$ be an integer and $C$ be a $B$-algebra. Let $[(A,\eta)]$ be a point in $ \mathrm{Ig}(N)(C)$ and $\omega$ be a basis  of $H^0(A,\omega_{A/C})$ over $C$.  A geometric modular form $f$ of weight $k$ on $\mathrm{Ig}(N)$ defined over $B$
is a rule that assigns to every triple $(A,\eta,\omega)$ over $C$,  a value $f(A,\eta,\omega)\in C$ such that the following conditions are met:
\begin{itemize}
\item[(G1)] $f(A,\eta,\omega)=f(A',\eta',\omega')\in C$ if $(A,\eta,\omega)\cong (A',\eta',\omega')$ over $C$.
\item[(G2)] For any  $B$-algebra homomorphism $\varphi:C\to C'$, we have
$f((A,\eta,\omega)\otimes_C C')=\varphi(f(A,\eta,\omega)).$
\item[(G3)] $f(A,\eta,t\omega)=t^{-k}f(A,\eta,\omega)$ for all $t\in C^\times$.
\item[(G4)] The value of $f({\rm Tate}(q),\eta_{\mathrm{can}},\omega_{\mathrm{can}})$ is an element of $ B  \llbracket q  \rrbracket$. This power series in 
$ B  \llbracket q  \rrbracket$
is called the algebraic Fourier expansion of $f$. 
\end{itemize}
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{prop:tensor}
    Let $f\in V_p(N,\mathcal{W})$  with $t$-expansion $f(t)$ around $x_\mathfrak{a}\otimes\bar{\mathbb{F}}_p$. Set
\[f_\mathfrak{a}(t):=f(t^{\mathrm{N}(\mathfrak{a})^{-1}\sqrt{-D_K}^{-1}}).\]
Suppose ${\varphi}:(\mathbb{Z}/p^n\mathbb{Z})^\times \mapsto \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{C}_p}^\times$ is a primitive Dirichlet character, then
\[f_\mathfrak{a}\otimes {\varphi}(x_\mathfrak{a})=p^{-n}\mathfrak{g}({\varphi})\sum_{u\in(\mathbb{Z}/p^n\mathbb{Z})^\times}{\varphi}^{-1}(u)\cdot f(x_\mathfrak{a}*\mathbf{n}(up^{-n})).\]
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- definition-2: body_md -->
Let 
$$\chi : K^\times \backslash \mathbb{A}^\times_K \to \mathbb{C}^\times$$
be a Hecke character.
\begin{enumerate}
\item We say that\textit{ $\chi$ has infinity type $(m,n)$}
if $$\chi_{\infty} (z) = z^m \overline{z}^n .$$
\item We say that \textit{$\chi$ is anticyclotomic} if $\chi(\mathbb{A}^\times_{\mathbb{Q}}) = 1$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end definition-2 -->
<!-- definition-3: body_md -->
\label{D:padicL}
Suppose $\psi$ is an anticyclotomic Hecke character of infinity type $(r,-r)$
 and let $c_0\mathcal{O}_K$ be the prime-to-$p$ part of the conductor of $\psi$. 
 Define the $p$-adic measure $\mathscr{L}_{{\mathfrak p},\psi}(f)$ on $\widetilde{\Gamma}$ by
\[\mathscr{L}_{{\mathfrak p},\psi}(f)(\rho)=\sum_{[\mathfrak{a}]\in \operatorname{Pic}\mathcal{O}_{c_0}}\psi(\mathfrak{a})\mathrm{N}(\mathfrak{a})^{-r}\cdot \left(\widehat{ f}^\flat_{\mathfrak{a}}\otimes\psi_{\mathfrak p}\rho|[\mathfrak{a}]\right)(A_\mathfrak{a},\eta_\mathfrak{a})\]
where $\rho \in \mathfrak{X}_{p^\infty}$.
We will view $\mathscr{L}_{{\mathfrak p},\psi}(f)$ as an element in the semi-local ring $\mathcal{W} \llbracket \widetilde{\Gamma} \rrbracket$.
<!-- end definition-3 -->
<!-- remark-1: body_md -->
In the definition of $\operatorname{Sel}^{\emptyset,0}(K,\mathbf{A})$ above, we have taken the trivial local conditions for primes away from $p$.
However, the standard BDP Selmer group (see example \cite{KobOta}) is defined using the unramified local conditions at primes away from $p$. The possible difference between these two local conditions only comes from primes dividing $N^-$ (see \cite[p. 1363, line 11]{Pollack_Weston_2011}). By \cite[Definition 3.3, Lemma 3.4]{Pollack_Weston_2011}, the hypothesis (\ref{Tam}) for primes dividing $N^-$ ensures that this difference is trivial and hence our definition of the BDP Selmer group coincides with the standard one.
<!-- end remark-1 -->
<!-- remark-2: body_md -->
This choice of $N^+$ and $N^-$ does not match with \cite[p. 575, line -1]{castella-hsieh-heegner-cycles} but matches with \cite{castella-wan-perrin-riou-ss} and hence we will assume henceforth that $(N, pD_K)=1$ so that it agrees with \cite[p. 575]{castella-hsieh-heegner-cycles}.
<!-- end remark-2 -->
<!-- head-1: body_md -->
\label{sec:ord}
 We make the following assumptions in the ordinary case.
 \begin{enumerate}
     \item $E[p]$ is irreducible as a $G_\mathbb{Q}$-module,
     \item the discriminant $D_K<0$ is odd,  and $D_K \neq -3$.
     \item every prime $\ell \mid N$ splits in $K$,
     \item $p$ splits in $K$ and $p >3$,
     \item $\bar{\rho}_E: G_\mathbb{Q} \rightarrow \mathrm{Aut}_{\mathbb{F}_p}(E[p])$ is surjective.
 \end{enumerate}
The following theorem is \cite[Theorem 1.2.4]{burungale-castella-skinner-gl2}.
\begin{theorem}\label{thm:main-conj-ord}
    Let $E/\mathbb{Q}$ has good ordinary reduction at $p$. Under the hypotheses (1)-(5) above, $X^{\emptyset,0}$ is $\Lambda$-torsion and $$\mathrm{Char}_{\Lambda}(X^{\emptyset,0})\Lambda^{\mathrm{ur}}=(\mathcal{L}_E)$$ as ideals in $\Lambda^{\mathrm{ur}}.$
\end{theorem}

\begin{remark}
    If $E[p]$ is reducible, then  we still have $\mathrm{Char}_{\Lambda}(X^{\emptyset,0})\Lambda^{\mathrm{ur}}=(\mathcal{L}_E)$ under certain hypotheses (cf. \cite[Theorem C]{CGLS2022}). 
\end{remark}
<!-- end head-1 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{thm:main-conj-ord}
    Let $E/\mathbb{Q}$ has good ordinary reduction at $p$. Under the hypotheses (1)-(5) above, $X^{\emptyset,0}$ is $\Lambda$-torsion and $$\mathrm{Char}_{\Lambda}(X^{\emptyset,0})\Lambda^{\mathrm{ur}}=(\mathcal{L}_E)$$ as ideals in $\Lambda^{\mathrm{ur}}.$
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- remark-3: body_md -->
If $E[p]$ is reducible, then  we still have $\mathrm{Char}_{\Lambda}(X^{\emptyset,0})\Lambda^{\mathrm{ur}}=(\mathcal{L}_E)$ under certain hypotheses (cf. \cite[Theorem C]{CGLS2022}).
<!-- end remark-3 -->
<!-- head-2: body_md -->
\label{sec:supersingular}
When $E/\mathbb{Q}$ has supersingular reduction at $p$, we assume the following conditions:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $N^-$ is the square-free product of an even number of primes.
\item $p$ splits in $K/\mathbb{Q}$ and write $(p) = \mathfrak{p} \overline{\mathfrak{p}}$ in $\mathcal{O}_K$
and $\mathfrak{p}$ is compatible with the choice of $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_p$.
\item $N$ is square-free.
\item There exists a prime $\ell$ dividing $N$ such that $\ell$ is non-split in $K/\mathbb{Q}$.
\item If $N$ is odd, then 2 splits in $K/\mathbb{Q}$.
\item $\overline{\rho}_E$ is ramified at every prime dividing $N^-$.
\end{enumerate}
\begin{theorem}\label{thm:main-conj-ss}
   Let $E$ has good supersingular reduction at $p$ with $a_p=p+1-\#\tilde{E}(\mathbb{F}_p)=0.$ Under the hypotheses (1)-(6) above, $X^{\emptyset,0}$ is $\Lambda$-torsion and $$\mathrm{Char}_{\Lambda}(X^{\emptyset,0})\Lambda^{\mathrm{ur}}=(\mathcal{L}_E)$$ as ideals in $\Lambda^{\mathrm{ur}}.$
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
   This follows by combining Theorem 5.3, Theorem 6.8 and Theorem A.5 of \cite{castella-wan-perrin-riou-ss}.
\end{proof}
<!-- end head-2 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
\label{thm:main-conj-ss}
   Let $E$ has good supersingular reduction at $p$ with $a_p=p+1-\#\tilde{E}(\mathbb{F}_p)=0.$ Under the hypotheses (1)-(6) above, $X^{\emptyset,0}$ is $\Lambda$-torsion and $$\mathrm{Char}_{\Lambda}(X^{\emptyset,0})\Lambda^{\mathrm{ur}}=(\mathcal{L}_E)$$ as ideals in $\Lambda^{\mathrm{ur}}.$
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
This follows by combining Theorem 5.3, Theorem 6.8 and Theorem A.5 of \cite{castella-wan-perrin-riou-ss}.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- theorem-4: body_md -->
\label{thm:control-theorem}
    Under \eqref{Tam} and \eqref{H^0}, one has that the natural homomorphism 
    $$\operatorname{Sel}^{\emptyset,0}(K_n,A) \rightarrow \operatorname{Sel}^{\emptyset,0}(K_\infty,A)^{\Gamma_n}$$ is an isomorphism.
<!-- end theorem-4 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
Suppose $E$ has supersingular reduction at $p$. Then we note that $A(K_\infty)$ and $A(K_{\infty,{\mathfrak p}^c})$ are both trivial from \cite[proof of Theorem 4.1]{LLMAdvances} and hence $A(K_\infty)$ and $A(K_{\infty,{\mathfrak p}^c}){}$ are also trivial. If $E$ has good ordinary reduction at $p$, then hypothesis \eqref{H^0} ensures that these groups are trivial. Therefore, the proof follows with the arguments exactly as in \textit{(loc.cit)}. We note that the failure of the surjectivity comes from the prime-to-$p$ local conditions and and this coincides with the ordinary case. Hypothesis \textbf{(Tam)} ensures that this failure vanishes (cf.  \cite[Proof of Theorem 3.9]{kim-kurihara}).
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- theorem-5: body_md -->
\label{thm:non-existence-finite}
    The $\Lambda$-submodule $\operatorname{Sel}^{\emptyset,0}(K_\infty,A)^\vee$ is $\Lambda$-torsion and does not contain any non-trivial finite submodule.
<!-- end theorem-5 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
The torsion-ness result follows from 
\cite[Theorem 1.6]{KobOta} which deals with both the ordinary and the non-ordinary cases simultaneously. Here we note that the Bloch-Kato Selmer groups in \textit{(loc.cit)} in in fact equal to our BDP Selmer group; thanks to \cite[p. 548, l. 1]{KobOta}, \cite[Remark 2.6]{KobOta} and \cite[p. 551, l. 14]{KobOta}. (See also the proof of Theorem 6.2 of \cite{castella-hsieh-heegner-cycles} which uses  \cite[Remark 2.6]{KobOta})

    The proof of the non-existence of finite submodule follows the same argument as laid by Greenberg in \cite[Prop. 4.14]{greenberg-lnm} (see also \cite[Lemma 3.4]{LMX} for the argument in the BDP-case which essentially follows Greenberg's original proof).
